title: Priority cannot bypass input

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that a task cannot start before its input exists, so a prerequisite goes first even when the task it feeds matters more

misconception: The most important task should always go first.
objective: Distinguish task priority from prerequisite readiness.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Which runs first? Which runs first? Correct option: The draft it needs. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.

claims.text: Stage: the review (10 min) is tagged high priority and needs the draft (20 min); send (5 min) needs the review. Review first, the review runs before the draft it needs; draft first, nothing runs before its input, and total waiting is 10 minutes more (50 against 40).

recall.question: 'Send invoice' is top priority but needs a signed quote first. Which order is possible?
options: Send the invoice first; it is top priority
Get the quote, then send the invoice
Do both at the same moment
recall.why: A priority label does not remove a prerequisite; the invoice cannot go before its input exists.
